question: On 9 October 2026, the United States placed the International Criminal Court (ICC) on the Office of Foreign Assets Control’s sanctions list, having already targeted several judges and officials. These sanctions threaten the Court’s operations, financial transactions, service providers and staff, undermining its independence and investigations, such as those focused on crimes committed in Palestine.

At the Foreign Affairs Council on 12 October 2026, Belgium and the Netherlands raised this issue. Kaja Kallas stated that the EU had several options to protect the ICC, without specifying them. Against this background: 1.
What concrete measures is the Commission considering to urgently protect the ICC, its staff and service providers from US sanctions, and when will it implement them?

In its reply to Written Question E-000718/2026) of 28 May 20261, the Commission stated it was considering revising the annex to Council Regulation (EC) No 2271/96 (the ‘Blocking Statute’)2 to explicitly include US sanctions against the ICC. What progress has been made since?

What guarantees will the Commission provide to European companies and financial institutions to maintain their relations with the ICC without suffering the extraterritorial effects of these sanctions?
